content.comment_body: Hello, could you please explain how to set up a photoresistor with [product_name] software? Is it possible to use inputs I1 and I2 as analog inputs for this connection? The requirement is: when it is dark, output Q1 should activate if input I3 receives a signal. If it's light, Q1 should remain off. Thank you!

I've attached a [document] containing a circuit diagram for connecting a photoresistor type "A 1060". The concept originates from a German blog: [url] In this setup, the LDR is in series with a voltage divider, and the analog input of the [product_name] is connected in parallel to the 4.7 kOhm resistor. Ensure both the voltage divider and the [product_name] operate with the same 24 VDC supply. Use an analog threshold switch within the software to set the point at which the output should trigger.

Could you clarify how you determined the resistor values in the diagram above? I have a similar scenario, but my photoresistor parameters differ: Illuminated 160 kOhm, Dimmed 3300 kOhm. I calculated resistor values of 115 and 240 kOhm. I'm unsure if my approach is correct.

The voltage divider, formed by R1 and R2, should be calculated so that when the LDR's resistance is close to 0 Ω, a voltage of about 10V appears across R2. Remember to factor in the internal resistance of the analog input on the [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users are requesting advice on how to integrate and program a photoresistor with a [product_name] controller using [product_name] software, specifically addressing wiring, analog input configuration, and logic based on sensor thresholds. There is some confusion about hardware connections and calculating resistor values for different photoresistor specifications, indicating a need for more detailed documentation or clearer software support for analog sensor integration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear, easy-to-follow instructions for wiring a photoresistor as an analog input and configuring the logic within [product_name] software. They also seek precise advice on choosing resistor values and setting up the program to achieve the intended output behavior.
